instruction: Start VLC, load the src.mp4 file located on the desktop, capture a 6-second segment starting at 00:02, and transform it into an animation.gif using GIMP.

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to use VLC to capture a 6-second clip starting at 00:02 from src.mp4 and convert it to an animated GIF named animation.gif using GIMP. The evaluator checks: (1) file exists at /home/user/Desktop/animation.gif, (2) file is a valid GIF format, (3) file size is between 1KB and 50MB, (4) GIF has at least 30 frames (animated), (5) GIF duration is approximately 6 seconds (5-7 second range). Note: Verifying the exact 00:02-00:08 portion of the source video is technically infeasible without frame-by-frame video comparison.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all feasibly-verifiable aspects of the instruction
Getter properly extracts GIF duration by iterating frames and summing frame durations (lines 51-65 in gimp.py getter)
Metric correctly validates duration is approximately 6 seconds using 5.0-7.0 second range with appropriate tolerance (20% of score)
Frame count threshold (min_frames=30) is appropriate for a 6-second animated GIF at typical frame rates
File existence, format validation, and size checks provide comprehensive verification
Scoring breakdown appropriately weights critical checks: file exists (25%), valid GIF (25%), duration (20%), frames (15%), size (15%)
Metadata correctly acknowledges technical limitation: verifying exact 00:02-00:08 source timestamps is infeasible without frame-by-frame comparison
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider tightening max_duration to 6.5 seconds instead of 7.0 for stricter verification, though current 5.0-7.0 range is acceptable
Minor: Could add width/height sanity checks to ensure GIF dimensions are reasonable (not 0x0 or excessively large), though current implementation already extracts these values
